_documentation.purpose: Reviewed research enrichment for the eight active catalogue records that had no citation-backed official details as of 2026-10-11, plus two evidence-backed deadline-display corrections. Every field below was read from the awarding body's own page on 2026-10-11 (see per-record citations and _evidence). Nothing here is inferred, completed or invented.
_documentation.scope: Local database only. The applier writes exclusively to the SQLite file passed to it as an argument. It never touches a production database, and the published snapshot is regenerated from the resulting local database.
_documentation.corpus_compatibility: Each record's 'official' and 'verification' objects use the same shape as backend/config/programme_details.json records, so a maintainer can fold them into the corpus and apply them through the usual maintenance path instead of this file.

records.title: DAAD University Summer Courses offered in Germany for Foreign Students and Graduates (HSK)

official.deadline_central_display: Applications 1 September to 30 October each year (23:59 CET)
official.funding_duration: Four-week language course, June to September
official.description: Four-week language, cultural and technical-language courses offered by German summer course institutions, in person only. Open to students and graduates in any subject area. Funded by the Federal Foreign Office. Course costs, single-room accommodation, country-specific travel allowance and health, accident and third-party liability insurance are also covered.
benefits: Health, accident and third-party liability insurance
coverage: Health, accident and third-party liability insurance
eligibility: Students and graduates in any subject area
Undergraduate applicants must have completed two academic years
Bachelor's, Master's or diploma degree holders
Funding for one course only
requirements: Apply through the DAAD portal, choosing three different course preferences
Completed application and supporting documents must reach the DAAD by the 30 October deadline
documents: Proof of German language proficiency (onSET, TestDaF, Goethe, DSD, DSH, telc or OeSD; B2 level, TDN 3, issued within the last two years) for German-taught courses

verification.source_freshness_rule: Course and contribution amounts are published annually; re-verify against the DAAD database entry each application cycle.

official.description: Doctoral scholarships for foreign doctoral students at German universities, funded by the Federal Foreign Office. Applicants must already be enrolled as doctoral students in Germany before the scholarship starts.

Already enrolled as a doctoral student in Germany
Good German language skills (B2), also accepted without a certificate
A concrete research plan is required
requirements: Apply as early as possible, ideally up to about two years before submission
Confirmation of supervision (Betreuungszusage) from the doctoral supervisor

records.title: Killam Predoctoral Scholarship (Dalhousie)
records.null_reason: The official Dalhousie page describes the Killam Predoctoral Scholarship as a cash stipend (up to $42,000 per year, $14,000 per term, plus relocation reimbursement, parental leave and research allowances) and does not state that tuition fees are covered. The stored column claimed tuition coverage, which the awarding body's own page does not support, so the claim is withdrawn: tuition_coverage is null - unconfirmed - until an official source states otherwise.
records.deadline_display: Round one: October 16, 2026 at midnight AT. Round two: opens December 1, 2026 - submissions due January 31, 2027 at midnight AT.

official.deadline_central_display: Round one: October 16, 2026 at midnight AT. Round two: opens December 1, 2026 - submissions due January 31, 2027 at midnight AT
official.funding_duration: Up to three years ($14,000 per term)
official.description: Dalhousie's Faculty of Graduate Studies offers a limited number of Killam Predoctoral Scholarships to high calibre students considering and pursuing doctoral studies. Open to Canadian and international students in all disciplines. Up to $42,000 per year for up to three years ($14,000 per term). Recipients are expected to apply for a Tri-agency Canada Graduate Scholarship - Doctoral (CGRS-D) within their first two years, in which case their award is topped up to $48,000 per year.
benefits: Up to $42,000 per year for up to three years ($14,000 per term)
$48,000 per year when held concurrently with a Tri-agency CGRS-D
Relocation allowance for new Killam Scholars
eligibility: Doctoral (PhD) students in all disciplines
Canadian and international students
One application per candidate
requirements: Expected to apply for a Tri-agency CGRS-D within the first two years
Annual report to the Faculty of Graduate Studies by 31 July
Apply through the FGS Scholarship Management Platform if not applying for CGRS-D
Confirm the offer by the stated deadline
documents: Completed FGS Scholarship Management Platform application

verification.source_freshness_rule: Dalhousie publishes the two application rounds each cycle; re-verify the round-two dates against the page.
verification.notes: The stored deadline_display said 'opens January 5, 2027, submissions due February ...' which the official page contradicts; it is corrected in this enrichment.

official.description: Economic support of $500.000 (CLP) per year toward the tuition (arancel) at an accredited higher-education institution, for children of education professionals and staff in municipal, state-subsidised or delegated schools, managed by the Ministerio de Educacion and the INCER.

New entrants: PAES score of at least 510 and NEM of at least 5.5
Continuing students: PAES 510 (or PDT/PSU 500) and 60% or 70% course approval
Within the 80% most vulnerable households (Registro Social de Hogares); PACE entrants are exempt from the ranking requirement

official.deadline_central_display: 2027 admission: apply through FUAS between 1 and 22 October 2026
official.description: A monetary contribution of between $600.000 and $860.000 (CLP) per academic year toward the tuition (arancel), managed by the Ministerio de Educacion and the INCER. Two modalities: Beca Nuevo Milenio up to $600.000 for the 70% lowest-income population, and Beca Nuevo Milenio II up to $860.000 for the 50% lowest-income population in institutions accredited for three years. There are 250 special places for students with disabilities.
benefits: Up to $600.000 (CLP) per academic year (Beca Nuevo Milenio)
Up to $860.000 (CLP) per academic year (Beca Nuevo Milenio II)
eligibility: Chilean nationals
First-year students within the 70% most vulnerable, with NEM of at least 5.0
No prior higher-education degree
Continuing students follow 60% or 70% course-approval thresholds
requirements: Apply through FUAS between 1 and 22 October 2026 for the 2027 admission
documents: FUAS application with RUT and ClaveUnica

verification.source_freshness_rule: Amounts, modalities and the FUAS window are published annually; re-verify against the ChileAtiende pagina when the 2027 cycle opens.
verification.notes: The published amount is a range (600.000 to 860.000 CLP per academic year) determined by income tranche and institutional accreditation. funding_amount is set to 600.000, the base modality, and the range is stated in the official detail so no reader sees the upper figure as the standard award.
